_note: Classical compute devices. int_ops / fp64_flops / fp16_flops are peak rates; 'sustained' fractions are applied by the model. Power: idle_w at zero load, tdp_w at full load, linear in between. tdp_w is MODULE-level power (the processor / accelerator module, boundary 1); 'system_overhead_ratio' is complete-server power divided by module power at rated maximum (boundary 2: CPUs, DRAM, NICs, fans/pumps, PSU losses), and facility power adds PUE and network on top (boundary 3). Entries marked vintage 'today' are calibration anchors; entries marked vintage 'mid2030s' are SCENARIOS (suffix _low / _high for slow / fast progress; the unsuffixed key is the base scenario), not products and not forecasts. Every entry has a 'source'; numbers without a cited source in it are assumptions. hbm_* fields are informational, except hbm_tbps which feeds the LLM-inference baseline (memory-bound decoding). 'llm_*' are not stored per device: see data/baselines.json.

gpu_2035.label: Accelerator module (base)
gpu_2035.source: SCENARIO, ASSUMPTION. Anchors (not extrapolation proofs): B200 1.0 kW (NVIDIA), MI355X up to 1.4 kW (AMD), Rubin reported at about 1.8 kW per board (Igor's Lab; unconfirmed, ~2.3 kW per GPU in another analyst source), Rubin Ultra / Kyber NVL576 rack about 600 kW planned for 2H 2027 (Jensen Huang at GTC, Data Center Dynamics), Google projects >500 kW per rack by 2030 and OCP Mt Diablo / NVIDIA 800 VDC target 1 MW racks, HBM4 22 TB/s per GPU on Rubin (vendor), KAIST TERALAB hypothetical HBM roadmap (not a vendor roadmap): ~75 W/stack HBM4, ~100-120 W HBM5, 180 W HBM8, ~8 TB/s per stack HBM6 and ~24 TB/s HBM7 (about 2035).
